s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and scotomas
salient_findings: Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms started in childhood
Night blindness is the only symptom reported
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision is normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
Electroretinogram shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Rod electroretinogram is flat
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

shortlist.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and scotomas

shortlist.label: Choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and marked inner retinal thickening

shortlist.label: Gyrate atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness, scotomas, and progressive visual impairment with normal color vision

shortlist.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood and marked retinal abnormalities

shortlist.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and supernormal thickness in perifoveal region

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and preserved visual acuity, along with the electroretinogram showing large, slow scotopic and photopic responses and a flat rod electroretinogram, are consistent with cone-rod dystrophy. The fundus examination and OCT findings also support this diagnosis, with the presence of few yellow spots, an indistinct grayish circle, and marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas.

rejected.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
rejected.why: Typically presents with more severe visual field loss and pigmentary degeneration on fundus examination

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Characterized by a more extensive loss of the choroid, retinal pigment epithelium, and photoreceptors, which is not consistent with the patient's preserved visual acuity and relatively mild fundus findings

rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with more pronounced myopia and a characteristic 'gyrate' pattern of atrophy on fundus examination, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with severe visual impairment or blindness at birth or in early infancy, which is not consistent with the patient's relatively preserved visual acuity
